definition: Robotic prosthesis control is a method for controlling a prosthesis in such a way that the controlled robotic prosthesis restores a biologically accurate gait to a person with a loss of limb.
details: This is a special branch of control that has an emphasis on the interaction between humans and robotics.

explainer.lead: Robotic prosthesis control steers a powered prosthesis so that it restores a biologically accurate gait for a person with limb loss. It matters because it sits at the human–robot interaction boundary.

tiers.eli5: It is the control system that makes a robotic artificial leg or arm move in a natural walking rhythm for the person wearing it.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers focus on the interaction between human and robotics, tuning control so motion matches natural gait. A pitfall is neglecting that interaction, since the wearer is part of the control loop.
tiers.paperLevel: Formally, it is a branch of control emphasizing human–robotics interaction, with the objective of a biologically accurate gait. Its scope is gait restoration for limb loss rather than general robot control.

explainer.example: A powered leg prosthesis is controlled so its stepping pattern matches a natural walking gait for the wearer.
